xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5078: Grok Build CLI harness: run Overdeck agents and conversations through xAI's grok (ACP)

plan.title: Grok Build CLI harness: run Overdeck agents and conversations through xAI's grok (ACP)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: Adding a literal to the Harness union forces coordinated edits across contracts, src/lib, CLI, dashboard server and frontend (type-forced Records plus hand-copied harness lists), and a harness that is selectable but not launchable delivers zero value. PAN-3668 (Prime Agent) kept the same full scope for the same reason. The work is decomposed into 24 small items with explicit dependency edges so leaves run in parallel.

narratives.Problem: Grok reaches Overdeck only as an outside bot plugin and as model ids through OpenCode Zen or the xai API-key provider. An operator with a signed-in Grok Build CLI (SuperGrok) cannot run Overdeck work agents, planning agents or conversations on it.
narratives.Proposal: Add a 'grok' harness that rides Overdeck's existing ACP host: a grok ACP provider entry launches 'grok agent --always-approve --no-leader stdio', authenticates with the cached sign-in, sets the model and reasoning_effort config options, resumes with session/load, and receives the managed overdeck MCP server through session/new. A new 'grok' model provider carries four grok/* ids that run only on the grok harness. The host records Grok's reported turn usage on the transcript, and a grok reconcile source imports it into the cost store. Pickers list Grok models when the CLI is installed and signed in; pan doctor reports missing or signed-out grok; docs cover setup and behavior.
narratives.NonGoals:
- A native terminal-UI grok harness or a companion terminal that attaches the Grok TUI to a conversation
- Running Grok agents on Fly machines
- Isolating GROK_HOME or filtering the operator's Grok MCP servers, plugins or hooks
- API-key (XAI_API_KEY) billing through the grok harness
- Dynamic model discovery from grok models
- Using grok agent serve, headless, leader mode, or any one-shot invocation (grok -p, --single, --prompt-file)
- Changing OpenCode's recorded session-index harness or recording OpenCode/Kimi ACP costs
- Adding grok to the lint-harness-branches pattern, raising any ratchet baseline, or raising any file-size allowlist row
- Reading Grok's private ~/.grok/sessions store
- Changing the xai provider or its bare grok-* model ids
- Adding a new HTTP route
- Distributing Overdeck skills or plugins into ~/.grok (pan sync targets, harness-skill-sync, Herdr integrations)

autoDecisions.summary: New harness literal 'grok' on the ACP host (OpenCode pattern), not a provider under the 'acp' harness
autoDecisions.rationale: harnessBinaryName('acp') and binaryConfigKey resolve the Kimi binary, capabilities (binaryLabel, installHint, npmPackage, updateArgs) are per harness, policy denies non-Kimi models on acp, and the issue's acceptance names harness grok in pickers.
The issue proposes 'harness: grok'; it matches the binary name and the existing telemetry mcp_client value.

autoDecisions.summary: New model provider 'grok' with prefixed ids grok/<cli-id> (grok-4.7, grok-4.7-build-fast, grok-4.6, grok-4.5), fixed union
autoDecisions.rationale: Auth and billing are provider properties: bare grok-4.7 is the xai API-key route. OpenCode keeps opencode/grok-4.7 separate the same way. grok models has no machine-readable output, so discovery is not used.

autoDecisions.summary: Launch 'grok agent --always-approve --no-leader stdio' and delete XAI_API_KEY from the child env
autoDecisions.rationale: --no-leader keeps one dedicated process per agent even when config enables leader mode; --always-approve mirrors OpenCode's pre-allowed permissions so Grok subagent asks cannot stall a turn; Grok's README says an API key takes precedence over the sign-in.

autoDecisions.summary: Cost = Grok's reported costUsdTicks / 1e10, pricing table as fallback; usage written to the ACP transcript and imported by a grok reconcile source
autoDecisions.rationale: The ticks matched the $2/$0.50/$6 and $4/$1/$12 rates exactly in probes and include the >=200K double rate the table cannot model; the transcript route avoids reading Grok's private session store.

autoDecisions.summary: Signed-in = ~/.grok/auth.json entry with a key and a future expires_at or a refresh_token
autoDecisions.rationale: grok models reported 'not authenticated' while ACP auth succeeded, and grok whoami/status need a TTY, so no subprocess is a reliable signal.
xAI's first-party CLI runs xAI models on the operator's own xAI sign-in, and its README documents ACP mode for custom automation tools.

autoDecisions.summary: Accept the operator's ~/.grok config (MCP servers, plugins, hooks) instead of isolating GROK_HOME
autoDecisions.rationale: Isolation would lose auth.json; Kimi and OpenCode also read their operator config.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the full scope in one issue with sizeJustification
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-3668 precedent: a Harness literal forces coordinated edits across five subsystems and a selectable but unlaunchable harness has no value; the work is split into 24 items with real edges.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not add 'grok' to the lint-harness-branches pattern
autoDecisions.rationale: Adding it would raise baseline rows, which is an operator decision; new behavior uses capability and provider-support fields instead of name comparisons.

Add readGrokSignIn, the auth.json sign-in reader

narrative.Action: PRD WI-13, D7. New src/lib/grok-sign-in.ts: export interface GrokSignIn { signedIn: boolean; reason: 'ok' | 'missing' | 'unreadable' | 'no-credential' | 'expired' } and async readGrokSignIn(home = homedir(), now = new Date()). Read join(home, '.grok', 'auth.json') with fs/promises readFile (no subprocess, no execSync). ENOENT -> missing; JSON parse error -> unreadable; no object value with a non-empty string key -> no-credential; a value with key and (Date.parse(expires_at) > now or a non-empty refresh_token) -> ok, signedIn true; otherwise expired. Never log or return token values. Tests use temp home dirs with synthetic fixtures only.
